rule: `self.m()` / `this.m()` / a bare call to a member of the enclosing type -> `Type#m`. | Each call in a multi-line method chain is reported on the line of its own method name, not the chain's first line. | Call on a computed receiver (call result, ...): `.member`
notes: Each `require` is an invocation of the loader: `_G#require`, medium, direct, on its line (Decisions 2026-11-10, CommonJS / Lua `require`). main.lua is not itself required; it sits at the require root (src/) that explains every require string in the case, so the name a require from that root gives it is `main` (Lua note: 'module = the name the scan's `require` strings give the file'). call_type convention (SPEC lists the types but gives no Lua mapping): a `:` call is method, a `.` or bare call is direct (the 2026-11-10 require ruling makes `_G#require` direct), a call through a value is callback. `self:validate()` in `function Q:build` names the enclosing table's member: `query#validate`, high. In the chain starting on line 22 each `:where`/`:build` is called on the previous call's result, a computed receiver, so `.where` / `.build`, low (Lua has no declared return types to type the result), each on its own line 23/24/25. `self.parts` and `#self.parts` are field access/operator.
